question: Can the PRRC 2019 label “Banak; Ludong” and its three Cestraeus name candidates be resolved to one fish species at its Pasig River stations using the 2014 and 2022 Ludong studies?

prrcLabelUnderReview.sourceLocator: Fish Tissue Analysis in the Pasig River System, PDF pages 6-8 (report footer pages 5-7), and Annex A on PDF page 16.
prrcLabelUnderReview.interpretation: The report presents multiple names together under a common-name/profile label; it does not provide an individual voucher, photo-to-name key, diagnostic measurements, or sequence that selects one of those names for a particular 2019 Pasig-system specimen. Preserve its exact wording as unresolved source alternatives.
prrcLabelUnderReview.stationLinks: The PRRC report gives historical station-level common-name catches and length entries, but this review does not treat the three-name Banak/Ludong profile as three independently identified taxa at every station.

2014MorphologicalStudy.citation: Ventolero, M. F. H., Ame, E. C., Catacutan, B. J. N., & Santos, M. D. (2014). Taxonomic identification of “Ludong” fish from the Cagayan River (Philippines). Philippine Science Letters, 7(1), 45-54.
sourceLocators: Journal landing page abstract and full article sections on sampling, morphological identification, results, and conclusion.
findings: The study concerns “Ludong” samples from Cagayan River and its tributaries, not an NCR waterbody.

The abstract reports at least Cestraeus oxyrhynchus and C. goldiei in Cagayan River; the article explains that morphology-based separation is difficult and discusses C. goldiei/C. plicatilis ambiguity among examined samples.
The study's morphological results are contextual evidence about a Cagayan sample set, not a specimen-level match to the separate 2019 PRRC Pasig samples.
2014MorphologicalStudy.reuseStatus: No open license or separate republication permission was identified on the article page; no figure, table, or specimen photograph is reused.

findings: The NFRDI study reports 20 newly collected samples plus seven archived sequences from the 2014 Ventolero study; 27 sequences were initially considered and 25 retained for analysis.

The paper reports all 25 retained CO1 sequences as Cestraeus goldiei. Its samples are from Cagayan River and tributaries in Cagayan/Isabela and one Abra River locality; none are from Pasig River or NCR.
Because seven archival sequences came from the 2014 study, the two articles are related research lineage and must not be counted as two wholly independent sample sets.

The 2022 paper discusses the disagreement with earlier morphology-based identifications and raises possible C. goldiei/C. oxyrhynchus synonymy as a hypothesis; it does not present a Pasig specimen or resolve the PRRC label.

The existing NFRDI/GenBank crosswalk documents four paper-versus-GenBank province conflicts, missing coordinates, and the absence of a permanent museum voucher crosswalk for the study codes. Those limits remain in force.
2022MolecularStudy.license: The NFRDI article states CC BY-NC 4.0. No app reuse is approved; its noncommercial license and image/table rights require separate review before any product use.

taxonomicDecision.decision: Unresolved for the PRRC 2019 Pasig-system samples.
taxonomicDecision.reason: The two taxonomic studies concern northern Luzon/Cordillera sample sets and include no voucher, tissue sequence, field-photo diagnostic, or sample-code bridge to the 2019 NCR fish. A common name and a regional taxonomic result cannot identify a different fish specimen.
doNotInfer: Do not replace the PRRC's multi-name profile with Cestraeus goldiei based on the 2022 northern study.
Do not count the 2014 and 2022 northern datasets as independent confirmation for the NCR sample.
Do not treat the regional Ludong literature as a Pasig River, Manila Bay, or Estero de San Miguel occurrence record.
Do not infer current presence, abundance, catchability, food safety, or fishing rules from these historical sources.

rightsAndEvidenceDecision.decision: Keep the evidence as an attributed research crosswalk. Do not copy the 2014/2022 article imagery, tables, or figures into Bangwit.

nextActions: Seek the PRRC 2019 field-identification notes, specimen vouchers, tissue sample codes, or genetic records that could link a Pasig fish to a named Cestraeus taxon.
If that specimen crosswalk is unavailable, retain the PRRC label as unresolved and continue NCR evidence work without assigning a species-level Banak/Ludong record.
Keep the existing NFRDI/GenBank sample-locality and noncommercial-license findings attached to any future reuse of the 2022 study.
